env.name: cmv
env.description:
Measure the supplied hypotheses; do not discover, rewrite or refine them. Each feature is
one scalar measurement of a discussion row, not a separate observation for every comment.
The full supplied corpus contains 2,000 rows: 1,000 changed and 1,000 unchanged outcomes.
Describe associations, not proven causal effects or prospective prediction.

Columns:
  - post_created_utc: Unix timestamp for the original post, not a comment or score-measurement
    timestamp. Response delay cannot be calculated from it.
  - title: the original poster's (OP's) heading or claim statement, not the argument body.
  - argument: the OP's explanation of their view. Use this field for argument-body measurements;
    include title only when the requested scope includes the heading or when it is needed to
    interpret a comment's target. Text can contain quotations, edits and outcome announcements.
  - OC_comments: a JSON-encoded list of available counter-argument comments by OTHER users,
    not the OP. Parse the list before counting comments, words or semantic instances.
    Specify any/all/count/share/mean explicitly. List order is not rank, importance or chronology.
    If properties must coexist in one comment, assess their conjunction within that comment;
    separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. The row-level extractor still returns one scalar.
    List length counts comments, not necessarily distinct commenters. No per-comment outcomes,
    scores or timestamps are supplied. OP-language measurements use title/argument instead.
  - conversation: formatted interaction text overlapping OC_comments, not extra independent
    evidence. It may include later replies and explicit view-change announcements. Do not use
    it as an initial-argument snapshot. When interaction is required, specify speaker/turn
    selection and use it only if faithful measurement is possible under the leakage guard below.
  - log_length: a supplied log-transformed length measure. Construction, source text, log base
    and timing are undocumented. When named by the hypothesis, use the supplied value and state
    that limitation; do not equate it with argument word count or reconstruct its log base.
  - post_score: the observed original-post score, not a comment score, voter count or initial
    endorsement. Its measurement time relative to the outcome is unknown; post_created_utc
    does not establish that timing.
  - delta: OUTCOME, 1 if the OP changed their view, else 0. Never a predictor or annotation input.
  - post_id, comment_id: identifiers, never predictors.

Attribution and unavailable measurements:
  - No measured personality scores, Big Five questionnaires or author demographics are supplied.
    A personality inference from writing is a linguistic proxy, not an observed trait; do not
    substitute it silently when the hypothesis requires an unavailable measurement.
  - Distinguish the author's own assertions or experiences from attributed quotations.
    An external source cited as support can count for an evidence feature without making the
    source's wording or experience the author's own. Background/rebuttal quotations are not
    automatically adopted support. Apply this distinction to OP text and other users' comments.
    Quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker.

Predictor leakage guard (applies to every text field):
  - Never use the OP's own view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or
    resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred as predictor evidence.
    This exclusion applies even inside argument and even if such text expresses the construct.
    Generic discussion of platform/delta rules is not an outcome announcement; retain relevant
    discussion rather than blanket-removing mentions of delta.
  - Subject to this guard, measure supplied current text unless the hypothesis restricts time.
    Deleting marked edits or outcome announcements does not reconstruct initial/pre-outcome
    text. Neither post_created_utc nor unordered comments supplies missing comment/edit times.
    An edit marker alone does not establish when an edit occurred.
    If faithful exposure requires unavailable temporal information, state that limitation and
    set term=null; do not substitute current text or infer a snapshot.
  - delta remains the fixed outcome. A hypothesis requiring another outcome or outcome-reporting
    text as a predictor is unsupported: explain the limitation and set term=null.
    If excluding outcome evidence changes the requested predictor itself, preserve the original
    claim as unsupported; do not silently replace it with a cleaned concession/attitude proxy.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.

features.name: op_argument_compares_to_established_scientific_or_historical_norms
features.definition: OP argument: 1 if the OP's own argument explicitly compares its claim or case to an established scientific or historical norm, standard, or precedent.
features.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, makes an explicit comparison between their claim/case and an established scientific norm (e.g., accepted scientific standard, consensus, or finding) or an established historical norm (e.g., historical standard, practice, or precedent); the comparison must be explicit, not merely a passing mention. Examples are nonexhaustive. Return 0 if no such comparison is present. Exclude quotations or positions attributed to others unless the OP adopts them. Exclude and never use OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if they contain comparisons; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot. If the argument is missing or malformed return null.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with op_argument_compares_to_established_scientific_or_historical_norms=1 have the same delta rate as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_argument_compares_to_established_scientific_or_historical_norms=1 have a lower delta rate than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Association only. Measures current argument text, not an initial snapshot; marked edits are retained but outcome announcements excluded. "Established norm" is judged semantically; no frequency or intensity cutoff.

decomposed.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.

features.name: op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation
features.definition: OP argument: the OP explicitly expresses their own fear of social rejection or isolation (e.g., being rejected, ostracized, excluded or left alone by others).
features.spec: Read only the OP's argument text. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly states fear, dread or worry of social rejection or social isolation (being rejected, ostracized, excluded, abandoned or left alone by other people) in connection with their view or its expression; return 0 if no such explicit fear is stated. Exclude quotations or reports of other people's fears or positions unless the OP adopts them as their own. Merely holding a view, being generally emotional, or discussing social topics without explicit personal fear of rejection/isolation gives 0. Ignore and never use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if inside the argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Measure the supplied current text including marked edits; do not try to reconstruct an initial version. If argument is missing or malformed return null.

features.name: op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense
features.definition: OP argument: the OP states their beliefs without any emotional self-defense (no defensive emotional protection of self, feelings or identity against criticism or rejection).
features.spec: Read only the OP's argument text. Return 1 if the OP states beliefs/claims and contains no emotional self-defense, i.e. no language that defensively protects the OP's feelings, identity or self-image against anticipated criticism, judgment, attack or rejection (e.g., pre-emptive pleas, fear-driven defensiveness, wounded or defensive self-justification). Return 0 if the argument contains any such emotional self-defense. Ignore other people's quoted positions unless adopted by the OP. Ignore and never use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if inside the argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Measure supplied current text including marked edits; do not reconstruct an initial version. If argument is missing or malformed return null.

decomposed.h0: View-change rate does not differ between arguments with op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation and arguments with op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense.
decomposed.h1: Arguments with op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation have lower view-change rates than arguments with op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense.
decomposed.note: The claim contrasts two named groups. A row can be neither (e.g., other emotional defense without fear of rejection) or, in principle, be coded fear=1 and no-self-defense=0 only; the two are not complements. In a joint model each coefficient is conditional on the other, so no single coefficient equals the fear-versus-no-self-defense contrast; hence term=null. Measures use current argument text (with marked edits) after excluding outcome announcements; timing is unknown. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.

features.name: any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent
features.definition: Other-user comments: at least one comment cites a specific, functioning institutional precedent (an actual existing institution, policy or system that operates in practice) as support.
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment cites a specific, actual institutional precedent that is functioning/operating in practice (e.g., a named existing law, policy, program, organization or country's system and how it works) as support for the comment's argument; 0 otherwise. Hypothetical or invented scenarios, purely abstract principles, and merely mentioning an institution without using its functioning as a precedent do not count. No external verification is required. Empty list -> 0; missing/malformed OC_comments -> null. List order carries no meaning. Ignore any text announcing the OP's view change or delta award, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered if relevant.  Output a single 0/1 value.

features.name: any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles
features.definition: Other-user comments: at least one comment relies on abstract normative principles (moral, rights or fairness argument).
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment relies on abstract normative principles, i.e. a moral, rights, justice or fairness argument about what ought to be, rather than on concrete cases; 0 otherwise. A comment that also cites concrete evidence still counts if it relies on an abstract normative principle. Empty list -> 0; missing/malformed OC_comments -> null. List order carries no meaning. Ignore any text announcing the OP's view change or delta award, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered if relevant. Output a single 0/1 value.

decomposed.h0: Rows with any comment citing functioning institutional precedents do not differ in delta probability from rows with any comment relying on abstract normative principles.
decomposed.h1: Any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent is associated with higher delta probability than any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles.
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast between two named styles (precedent vs abstract normative). Both are measured, but a row can have both or neither, and in the OLS the coefficient on the precedent feature is conditional on the normative one, not the difference beta_A - beta_B; no single available coefficient represents the contrast, so term=null. 'Counter-arguments' is operationalized at row level as any-comment presence; the hypothesis does not specify any/share. Comment-level outcomes are not available.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring longer precomputed log-transformed discussion length are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: supplied_log_length
features.definition: Discussion row: the supplied precomputed log-transformed length value (log_length), used as given.
features.spec: df['log_length'] converted with pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce'); return as float, null if missing or non-numeric. Observed range about 0.69-7.44. Construction, source text, log base and timing are undocumented; do not recompute or equate with word count.

decomposed.h0: supplied_log_length has no association with the likelihood of delta (OP view change).
decomposed.h1: Higher supplied_log_length is associated with a higher likelihood of delta.
decomposed.note: log_length is a supplied value with undocumented construction, source text, log base and timing relative to the outcome; it may include post-outcome text, so it is not verified as pre-outcome. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit admissions of uncertainty are associated with a higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty.

features.name: op_argument_explicit_uncertainty_admission
features.definition: OP argument: 1 if the OP explicitly admits uncertainty or possible error about their own view or claims (own stance, not quoted others).
features.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly admits uncertainty, doubt, or possible error about their view or claims (e.g., 'I might be wrong', 'I'm not sure', 'I'm unsure whether'); otherwise 0. Exclude quoted or reported text from others unless the OP adopts it, and exclude moderator/bot notices. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred (e.g., 'my view was changed', 'Δ'); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot or remove edits. Missing or malformed argument -> null; an assessable argument with no such admission -> 0.

features.name: op_argument_asserts_absolute_certainty
features.definition: OP argument: 1 if the OP explicitly asserts absolute certainty about their own view (no doubt possible).
features.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly asserts absolute certainty about their view or claims (e.g., 'I am 100% certain', 'there is no possible doubt', 'undeniably, absolutely true'); ordinary confident phrasing without a claim of absolute certainty gives 0. Exclude quoted or reported text from others unless the OP adopts it, and moderator/bot notices. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot or remove edits. Missing or malformed argument -> null; an assessable argument without such assertion -> 0.

decomposed.h0: Rows whose OP argument admits uncertainty (op_argument_explicit_uncertainty_admission) have the same view-change probability as rows asserting absolute certainty (op_argument_asserts_absolute_certainty).
decomposed.h1: Rows with op_argument_explicit_uncertainty_admission have higher view-change probability than rows with op_argument_asserts_absolute_certainty.
decomposed.note: The claim contrasts two named groups (uncertainty admission vs absolute certainty). Both are measured, but they are not complements: a row can show both or neither. In the additive model, the uncertainty coefficient is conditional on certainty and does not equal the uncertainty-versus-certainty contrast. No single available coefficient represents the claim, so term=null. Measurement uses current argument text, including marked edits, with outcome announcements excluded. No initial snapshot is reconstructed, and edit timing is unavailable. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises within the argument are positively associated with view change.

features.name: share_comments_challenging_multiple_factual_premises
features.definition: Other-user comments: share of comments that each challenge two or more distinct factual premises of the OP's argument.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP). Use title and argument as context to identify the OP's factual premises (empirical/descriptive claims about how the world is, not values or logical-structure claims). For each comment, decide whether it challenges (disputes, contradicts, or presents evidence against) at least two distinct factual premises stated in the OP's argument/title; challenging one premise, or only value/normative/logical claims, does not qualify. Two challenges to the same premise count once. Count the premises within the same comment only. Return the number of qualifying comments divided by the total number of comments, a number from 0 to 1. Empty list: null. Missing or malformed OC_comments, title or argument: null. Ignore as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, including inside argument or comments; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Use current supplied text; list order carries no meaning. Do not use conversation.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_challenging_multiple_factual_premises has no association with delta.
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_challenging_multiple_factual_premises is positively associated with delta.
decomposed.note: "Frequently" has no specified cutoff; operationalized as the share of comments (a continuous measure), with no threshold chosen. "Multiple" interpreted as two or more distinct premises. Uses current text; comment order/timing unavailable. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: oc_comment_count
features.definition: OC_comments: number of counter-argument comments by other users in the parsed list.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list (json.loads). Return len(list) as a non-negative integer count of comments (not distinct commenters). A valid empty list gives 0; missing or malformed JSON gives null. Does not read text content, so no outcome announcement content is used.

decomposed.h0: oc_comment_count has no association with the likelihood of delta (OP changing view).
decomposed.h1: Higher oc_comment_count is associated with a higher likelihood of delta (fewer comments, lower likelihood).
decomposed.note: Interpreted "original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses" as the number of available OC_comments for the row. OC_comments is a supplied list of available comments and may not be the complete thread; list order and timing are unavailable. Association only, linear probability/OLS on the binary outcome.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: distinct_counterargument_count
features.definition: OC_comments (other users): number of semantically distinct counter-arguments against the OP's view across all comments, counting a repeated argument once.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; order is not rank or chronology). Use title and argument only as context to identify the OP's view that comments oppose. Count the number of distinct counter-arguments, i.e. separate substantive reasons, evidence points or premises challenging the OP's view, across all comments combined. Deduplicate semantically: the same argument made in several comments or restated within a comment counts once; one comment may contain several distinct counter-arguments. Do not count questions, agreement, jokes, clarification requests, or points not opposing the OP's view. Exclude any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, wherever they appear (including argument or comments); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered if relevant. Use current supplied text; do not reconstruct an initial snapshot. Output a non-negative integer. A valid empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null; missing OP title/argument preventing identification of the OP's view gives null.

features.name: has_at_least_three_distinct_counterarguments
features.definition: OC_comments: 1 if there are at least three semantically distinct counter-arguments to the OP's view, else 0.
features.spec: Using `distinct_counterargument_count`: return null if df['distinct_counterargument_count'] is null; else 1 if df['distinct_counterargument_count'] >= 3, else 0.

decomposed.h0: has_at_least_three_distinct_counterarguments has no association with delta.
decomposed.h1: Rows with has_at_least_three_distinct_counterarguments=1 have a higher likelihood of delta=1 than rows with 0.
decomposed.note: Association only. Distinctness of counter-arguments is a semantic judgment aggregated across all comments (deduplicated across comments). OC_comments is only the available posted comments; list order carries no chronology. Current text is used; no initial snapshot is reconstructed. Binary feature is derived from the count feature (the count feature is a prompt, the threshold >=3 is code).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post title uses absolute certainty markers are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: title_uses_absolute_certainty_markers
features.definition: OP title: 1 if the title itself uses absolute certainty markers (e.g., universal or categorical wording expressing no possible doubt or exception), else 0.
features.spec: Read only the title column (the OP's heading). Return 1 if the title's own wording uses at least one absolute certainty marker, i.e. language asserting the claim with complete certainty or without exception or doubt (such as universal quantifiers like all/every/always/never/no one, categorical claims like 'definitely', 'obviously', 'undeniably', 'impossible', 'literally'/'completely' used to assert certainty). Examples are nonexhaustive. Return 0 if the title has no such markers, including hedged or tentative wording ('generally', 'I think', 'maybe'), or merely stating an opinion or 'should' claim without absolute certainty wording. Ignore the 'CMV:' prefix. Do not use argument, comments or conversation. Exclude any text in the title announcing a view change or delta award or reporting outcomes (not expected in titles); generic platform/delta-rule mentions are not outcome announcements. If the title is missing or empty, return null.

decomposed.h0: title_uses_absolute_certainty_markers has no association with delta (coefficient is zero).
decomposed.h1: title_uses_absolute_certainty_markers is associated with a lower likelihood of delta (negative coefficient).
decomposed.note: Title is current supplied text; the comparison group is titles without absolute certainty markers. Association only, not causal. The qualifying marker set is a semantic judgment without a fixed lexicon.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where original posts explicitly invite critique or use tentative language are associated with higher view-change rates than those using absolute, definitive declarations.

features.name: op_invites_critique_or_uses_tentative_language
features.definition: OP title/argument: 1 if the OP explicitly invites critique/challenge to their view or uses tentative, hedged language about their own claims.
features.spec: Read the OP's title and argument (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly invites critique, challenge or counterarguments to their view (e.g. asking to be convinced or shown wrong) OR uses tentative/hedged language about their own position or claims (e.g. 'I might be wrong', 'I think', 'perhaps', 'to my knowledge'). Return 0 if neither is present. Ignore external quotations and other speakers' text unless the OP adopts them. Standard 'CMV' title prefix alone does not count. Exclude and do not use as evidence any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even inside argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot. Return null if title and argument are both missing or empty/malformed.

features.name: op_uses_absolute_definitive_declarations
features.definition: OP title/argument: 1 if the OP states their own view using absolute, definitive declarations (certainty, universal claims, no acknowledged doubt).
features.spec: Read the OP's title and argument (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, states their view or claims with absolute, definitive declarations, i.e. expressed certainty or categorical/universal assertions presented without hedging (e.g. 'all', 'always', 'never', 'undeniably', 'obviously', flat declarative claims of fact). Return 0 if no such absolute declarations are present. This is not the complement of tentativeness: a row may be 0 on this measure and also lack tentative language, or can contain both. Ignore external quotations and other speakers' text unless the OP adopts them. Exclude and do not use as evidence any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even inside argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot. Return null if title and argument are both missing or empty/malformed.

decomposed.h0: View-change rates do not differ between discussions whose OPs invite critique or use tentative language (op_invites_critique_or_uses_tentative_language) and those using absolute definitive declarations (op_uses_absolute_definitive_declarations).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_invites_critique_or_uses_tentative_language have higher view-change rates than discussions with op_uses_absolute_definitive_declarations.
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast between two named groups; a row can be both, or neither, so neither is the complement of the other. In the additive model, the coefficient on either feature is conditional on the other and no single coefficient equals beta_tentative minus beta_absolute, so term=null (contrast not expressible as one coefficient). Measurements use current text including edits after the leakage exclusion; no initial snapshot is reconstructed. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that explicitly cite specific real-world examples are associated with higher likelihood of original view change.

features.name: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example
features.definition: Other-user comments: at least one comment explicitly cites a specific real-world example (an actual case, including a specific personal experience, not an invented hypothetical).
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly cites a specific real-world example, i.e. a concrete actual case, event, person, institution, study, or specific personal experience offered in the comment's argument. Invented or hypothetical scenarios and purely general claims do not count; no external verification is needed; examples need not be institutional or public. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment does so. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution text, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Moderator/bot notices do not count. List order carries no meaning.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example has no association with the probability of delta.
decomposed.h1: Rows with any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example=1 have higher probability of delta.
decomposed.note: "Discussions featuring" interpreted as at least one counter-argument comment citing such an example (any, no frequency cutoff specified). Comments are unordered; association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counterarguments containing measured, logical reasoning are positively associated with the original poster changing their mind compared to those containing emotional aggression in ChangeMyView discussions.

features.name: any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning
features.definition: Other-user comments: at least one counterargument uses measured, calm logical reasoning (reasoned argument in a composed, non-hostile tone).
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it; list order is not rank or chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment presents measured, logical reasoning: a reasoned argument or evidence-based inference stated in a calm, composed, non-hostile tone. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment does. Empty valid list -> 0. Missing or malformed input -> null. Assess each comment on its own text; quoted OP text or quoted others are not the commenter's reasoning unless adopted. A comment that is both logical and aggressive does not qualify as measured. Ignore and do not use any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution text, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, wherever it appears; generic discussion of delta/platform rules remains eligible. Output a single 0/1 per row.

features.name: any_comment_emotional_aggression
features.definition: Other-user comments: at least one counterargument contains emotional aggression (hostile, insulting, or angrily attacking language).
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it; list order is not rank or chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment contains emotional aggression: hostile, insulting, contemptuous, or angrily attacking language directed at the OP or their view. Mere disagreement, politeness-free bluntness, or generic emotional wording without hostility does not count. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment does. Empty valid list -> 0. Missing or malformed input -> null. Quoted text from others is not the commenter's own aggression unless adopted. Ignore and do not use any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution text, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, wherever it appears; generic discussion of delta/platform rules remains eligible. Output a single 0/1 per row.

decomposed.h0: Given any_comment_emotional_aggression, any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning is not associated with delta, and the measured-logical versus emotionally-aggressive contrast is zero.
decomposed.h1: Rows with measured logical counterarguments have higher delta rates than rows with emotionally aggressive counterarguments.
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast between two named comment styles. Both are measured, but the beta for measured reasoning in this model is conditional on aggression, not the difference beta_logical - beta_aggressive, so no single coefficient represents the claim and term=null. A row can have both, or neither, so no-aggression is not the same as measured reasoning. Row-level any-comment aggregation is an assumption, since the hypothesis doesn't specify any/share. OC_comments is unordered and has no per-comment outcomes.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific factual claims in the original post are associated with higher rates of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim
features.definition: Other-user comments: at least one single comment both directly quotes a specific factual claim from the OP's title/argument and refutes that same claim.
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP context) and OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment, within that same comment, explicitly quotes (verbatim or clearly marked quotation, e.g. > quote markup or quotation marks) a specific factual claim that appears in the OP's title or argument AND argues that this same claim is factually wrong or refutes it. Quotation and refutation must be in the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Quotations of non-factual claims (pure opinions/values), quotes without refutation, and refutation without quoting do not qualify. Ignore OP text that is an announcement of view change/delta award, post-outcome thank-you/resolution update, or any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; do not use it as the quoted claim or as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Use current supplied text including marked edits; do not infer initial snapshots. Return 0 if the list is valid and empty or no comment qualifies.
